header.account: A US criminal and traffic defense law firm
header.production_capacity: about 6 new lines a week, a few photos, no video

summary: The traffic can decide 4 tests this quarter, not dozens: two lanes of campaigns, about 5 weeks per test, each decided on CTR at a 30% minimum lift.
Every lane A and B campaign is on Maximize Conversions, so Google rotates ads for performance: each test runs as a 50/50 custom experiment, not as two ads in one ad group.
Fix first: 4 DUI ads carry drug-possession descriptions.
What wins today: question headlines (index 121) and proof, availability and number-led descriptions; but the question evidence comes almost only from traffic campaigns.

First tests: both lanes open with the firm's track record ('[N]+ Charges Resolved' pinned to headline 1), a description angle that leads the account but has barely run as a headline; then the same claim as a question.
Missing: no headline names an outcome, confidentiality, honesty, speed or what happens next, and only one non-brand campaign has image assets.

what_wins.method: click index = 100 x clicks / (impressions x the line's own ad CTR), non-brand, pinned lines left out; leading/lagging need 3,000+ impressions and |z| >= 2
what_wins.evidence_caveat: Question headlines: 8046 of 8439 impressions come from lane B (traffic) campaigns and 11 from lane A, so the lead is unproven for criminal, DUI and drug ads. Google picks which lines show, so every verdict here is a lead to test, not proof.

gaps.concept: Problem-solution: what happens next, step by step
Cost clarity: fees stated up front
Empathy: you are not alone / no judgement

testing_capacity.method: n per arm from the two-proportion formula, 95% two-sided, 80% power; weeks = 2 x n / weekly volume; slot = weeks rounded up, at least 2
testing_capacity.budget_rule_of_thumb_vs_traffic: Monthly spend is about $5,660. A budget table would allow 2-3 tests a week; the traffic decides about 4 a quarter at a 30% MDE.

week_0_fixes: Replace the 4 drug-possession descriptions in the 4 DUI ads with DUI descriptions the account already runs (for example 'Don't let a DUI conviction ruin your job, record and future. [N]+ 5 Star Client Reviews.'). Lane A tests the DUI campaign, so the mistake must go first. You make this change in Google Ads; this skill has no action that edits ad text.

Create the experiments for A1 and B1 in Google Ads (one per campaign, 50/50). In each trial arm, pin '[N]+ Charges Resolved' to headline 1 (adding the line where the ad doesn't have it), then start them together.
roadmap.lane_C: No tests: 28.6 weeks for one CTR test at a 30% MDE. These campaigns take each winner once it is decided in lane A or B.

tests.the_one_change: the angle of the opener: pin '[N]+ Charges Resolved' (proof by track record) to headline 1, replacing any line pinned there today
tests.hypothesis: If the ads open with the firm's track record, CTR rises by at least 30%, because track-record descriptions lead the account and the line beats its own ads' CTR in lane A when Google shows it (on thin volume so far).
tests.evidence: track record: descriptions account-wide 5476 impressions, index 113, z 3.2 (leading); lane A headlines 1602 impressions, index 132, z 3.0 (thin); every lane A ad already carries a track-record headline, unpinned
tests.how_it_runs: Google Ads custom experiment per campaign, 50/50 split; the variant ad goes in the trial arm (all lane campaigns are on Maximize Conversions, so two ads in one ad group would not be a fair split)
tests.guardrail: conversions per click (baseline 21.2%): a no-harm check only, since it needs 16.4 weeks to reach its own sample
variants: variant: the same lines with '[N]+ Charges Resolved' pinned to headline 1 (in place of the ad's own track-record headline where its wording differs)
tests.notes: A confirmation test: the lead comes from descriptions and from lane B; lane A's own headline read is thin.
tests.stop_rules: run until both arms reach the impressions per arm and 14+ days have passed; stop early only if the variant is disapproved, doesn't serve, or its conversions per click fall under half the control's once each arm has 100+ clicks

budget.why: Each experiment splits its campaign's existing budget 50/50.
budget.traffic_on_variants: weeks 1-10: about 47.8% of non-brand impressions see a variant
budget.smaller_split_option: a 30/70 split in lane A would need about 7.2 weeks per test instead of 4.3

decision_rules.run_until: both arms reach the impressions per arm and 14+ days have passed; stop early only for a disapproved or non-serving variant, or a collapsed guardrail (variant conversions per click under half the control's once each arm has 100+ clicks)
decision_rules.winner: CTR better at p < 0.05 (two-proportion z-test) and conversions per click not clearly worse: roll out, then queue 3 iterations
decision_rules.no_clear_difference: keep the control, log it, make the next variant bolder
decision_rules.loser: log what it taught; consider the opposite idea
